issues.failure_explanation: The abstract advertises that "optimal strong convergence rates ... are derived for the Euler--Maruyama methods" and the introduction claims Section~4 shows "optimality of the rate". The paper establishes only upper error bounds (Theorems Thm:ConvEM and Thm:ConvEM2); no lower bound, sharpness example, or matching comparison appears anywhere in the source, so optimality of the rates is never proved.

failure_location.quote: In Section~\ref{Sec:4}, the Euler--Maruyama scheme is analyzed, showing optimality of the rate and the convergence to the continuous solution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the optimality claims in the abstract and the introduction, or add a genuine matching lower-bound/sharpness argument for the derived rates.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that the derived strong/weak Euler--Maruyama rates are optimal is unsupported; the upper-bound rates of Theorems Thm:ConvEM and Thm:ConvEM2 themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Unsupported claim of optimal Euler--Maruyama rates
issues.why_classification: All proved upper bounds survive unchanged, but the repair necessarily withdraws a promised guarantee about the rates; proving optimality would need an essentially new lower-bound argument, so the resolution is a limited weakening rather than a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The real-valued spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$.
Inhere $(P_{\ell,m})_{\ell\in\N_0, m\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}}$ are the associated Legendre polynomials.

issues.failure_explanation: The m<0 branch of the definition of $\realSH_{\ell,m}$ is the scalar expression $(|m|\varphi)$: it is independent of $\vartheta$, contains no factor $P_{\ell,|m|}$ (although $(P_{\ell,m})$ is defined only for $m\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}$) and no normalization, and $\varphi$ is not a globally defined function on $\S^2$. As defined the family is neither orthonormal nor complete, so the stated claim that it is an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$ is false and all expansions in this basis are ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Complete the m<0 branch with the real spherical harmonic proportional to $P_{\ell,|m|}(\cos\vartheta)\cos(|m|\varphi)$ with the normalization forced by orthonormality (or redefine the family as normalized real linear combinations of the complex spherical harmonics).
issues.overall_effect: Every harmonic expansion and every orthonormality/Parseval computation (noise expansion (eq:KL-expansion_Levy), solution series (eq:SolSeries2), and the moment and error computations in Lemma L:MESol, Theorems L:SA1, weakr, Thm:ConvEM, Thm:ConvEM2) is built on the displayed family and is ill-defined until the definition is completed.
issues.title: Malformed definition of real spherical harmonics for m<0
issues.why_classification: The intended basis is standard and its normalization is forced by orthonormality, so a local completion of one branch of the definition restores the basis property and all subsequent computations without any new argument or lost claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we used that $\widetilde{\mathcal{Y}}$ is an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$ and $X^0$ is independent of~$L$.

issues.failure_explanation: The second-moment identity drops every covariance term between $X^0$ and $L$, rewriting $\E[(X^0_{\ell,m}e^{-\ell(\ell+1)t}+\int_0^t e^{-\ell(\ell+1)(t-s)}dL_{\ell,m}(s))^2]$ as $\E[(X^0_{\ell,m}e^{-\ell(\ell+1)t}+\meanlm\int_0^t e^{-\ell(\ell+1)(t-s)}ds)^2]+\varlm\int_0^t e^{-2\ell(\ell+1)(t-s)}ds$, and the proof explicitly invokes the unstated fact that "$X^0$ is independent of $L$". The standing hypotheses only make $X^0$ $\mathcal{F}_0$-measurable and require $L$ to have independent increments; they do not exclude $\mathcal{F}_0$ carrying information about $L$. If e.g. $X^0=L_{0,0}(1)$, the factors $\E[X^0_{\ell,m}\int\cdots dL_{\ell,m}]$ do not split and the displayed identities are false. The same factorization is used in (eq:second-mom_EM).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and the lower bound of the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality \cite[Theorem~3.50]{peszat2007} implies
which is finite since $L\in  L^p(\Omega,H^\eta(\S^2))$ with

issues.failure_explanation: In case (ii) with p>2 the proof needs $\sum_{\ell,m}(1+\ell(\ell+1))^{\eta p/2}(\varlm^{p/2}+|\meanlm|^p)<\infty$ and derives it from $L\in L^p(\Omega,H^\eta)$ through the chain $\E|L_{\ell,m}(1)|^p\ge\E|L_{\ell,m}(1)-\meanlm|^p+|\meanlm|^p\ge C(\varlm^{p/2}+|\meanlm|^p)$. The first inequality is false for p>1: for a compound Poisson component with $\P(L_{\ell,m}(1)=0)=1-\epsilon$, $\P(L_{\ell,m}(1)=1/\epsilon)=\epsilon$ one has $\meanlm=1$, $\E|L_{\ell,m}(1)|^p\approx\epsilon^{1-p}$ but $\E|L_{\ell,m}(1)-\meanlm|^p+|\meanlm|^p\approx\epsilon^{1-p}+2$. Hence the summability needed for the $L^p$-regularity bound is not established by the given argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false additive inequality by the valid bound $\E|Z|^p\ge\max\{|\E Z|^p,2^{-p}\E|Z-\E Z|^p\}\ge C_p(\varlm^{p/2}+|\meanlm|^p)$ (Jensen plus the two-sided Burkholder--Davis--Gundy bound already cited); the required summability then follows as written.
issues.overall_effect: The $L^p(\Omega,H^\rho)$ bound of Proposition prop:regul in case (ii) with p>2 (independent non-Gaussian components) is unproven, and with it the justification that the test-function class of Assumption ass:TestFunc is non-trivial and the weak rates of Corollary cor:added-1 in that regime.
issues.title: False moment inequality in the proof of the L^p regularity estimate
issues.why_classification: The needed conclusion is true and follows from the same cited tools in a couple of lines with an extra constant depending on p, so the regularity statement, its rates and all dependent claims survive with no new lemma or construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $X$ and $X^{(\kappa)}$, given by~\eqref{eq:SolSeries2} and~\eqref{eq:ApproxSpace}, respectively, and $\varphi$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:TestFunc} for some $\rho \ge 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:added-1 asserts the weak error bound for every $\varphi$ with derivative growth of arbitrary degree m, but assumes only $L\in L^p(\Omega,H^\eta)$ for one p and the standing $X^0\in L^2(\Omega,L^2)$. Theorem weakr applies only under Assumption ass:TestFunc at the index $\rho$ used in the rate, and the paper's own verification of that assumption requires $X(t)\in L^{2m}(\Omega,H^\rho(\S^2))$, which Proposition prop:regul yields only when $X^0\in L^{2m}(\Omega,H^\nu)$ and $L\in L^{2m}(\Omega,H^\eta)$. With $X^0$ having only two moments and $\varphi(x)=\|x\|^4_{L^2(\S^2)}$ (growth degree m=3, needing $X\in L^6$), $\E[\varphi(X(t))]$ can be infinite, so the asserted weak error need not exist at all.
